title: Ways to Earn Small

cards.aki: You do not need money to get into web3. You need to be useful.
cards.title: Ways to Earn Small
text: Five ways people earn their first crypto: content, airdrops, writing, videos and internships.
None of them make you rich overnight. All of them build skills and a reputation.

cards.aki: Content is how most people in web3 get noticed.
cards.title: Content creation

items.back: Short posts on X that explain one thing simply. Projects share good ones and sometimes pay for them.
Communities love good memes. Some projects run meme contests with token prizes.
A weekly roundup of one niche builds an audience that sponsors and projects will pay to reach.
Share what you learn as you go. It is a portfolio and a network at the same time.

cards.aki: Airdrops are real, but they are not free money.
cards.title: Airdrops
text: Projects sometimes reward early users with free tokens, called an airdrop, to spread ownership and say thank you.
points: Use new products for real, early on: test networks, apps and points programs.
It costs time, and sometimes fees. Many people spend more than they get.
Projects filter out farmers running lots of fake accounts.
Fake claim sites are everywhere. A real airdrop never asks you to pay first.

cards.title: A site says you can claim a big airdrop if you pay a small fee first. What is it?

options.text: A normal way to claim airdrops
options.why: Real airdrops never ask you to pay to claim.
Yes. The fee is the scam, and the airdrop never arrives. The site may also try to drain your wallet.

options.text: A good deal if the fee is small
options.why: The size of the fee does not matter. Paying to receive is the classic trick.

cards.aki: If you can write clearly, web3 needs you.
cards.title: Writing
points: Docs and guides: many projects pay for clear documentation and tutorials.
Research: deep dives into projects for funds, media and research groups.
Ghostwriting: threads and articles for founders who are too busy to write.
Community recaps: summaries of calls and governance votes.
cards.tip: Publish samples on a blog or onchain writing platform like Paragraph, so people can see your work before they hire you.

cards.aki: Not a writer? Try the camera.
cards.title: Videos

items.back: Short videos that explain one idea simply, on YouTube, TikTok or Shorts.
Screen recordings showing how to use a product step by step. Projects often pay for these.
Hosting livestreams or X Spaces with founders builds a network fast.
Many creators need editors. It is a skill you can sell straight away.

cards.aki: Here is a simple path to your first internship or gig.
cards.title: Internships and first gigs

steps.label: 1. Pick one ecosystem
steps.text: Choose one community, like Ethereum, Solana or a project you like, and get to know it well.

steps.label: 2. Help out for real
steps.text: Answer questions, write a guide, report bugs or translate docs. People notice who shows up.

steps.label: 3. Keep a proof of work list
steps.text: Collect links to everything you did. It becomes your CV.

steps.label: 4. Apply and reach out
steps.text: Use web3 job boards like web3.career or CryptoJobsList, and message teams directly with your work attached.

cards.title: Earn safely
points: Never pay to get a job, a training course with a promised job, or an activation fee.
Use a separate wallet for testing new apps and claiming rewards.
Ask to be paid in a well-known stablecoin, and check the network.
Keep records. In many countries crypto income is taxed.

cards.title: What is the best way to land your first web3 internship?

options.text: Show public work you have already done for the community
options.why: Yes. A link to real work beats any CV line.

options.text: Pay a recruiter a fee to guarantee a job
options.why: Real jobs never charge you. That is a scam.
Nobody knows everything. Start helping now and learn on the way.

cards.aki: Small wins add up. Go make something.
cards.title: Quick recap
points: Content: threads, memes, newsletters, building in public.
Airdrops: use products early, never pay to claim.
Writing and videos: projects pay for clear explainers and tutorials.
Internships: pick one ecosystem, help for real, keep proof of your work.
